Stockpile a ton away. It's like every other skill, once you want to start boosting these up, stockpile as much
resources as you can prior to actually committing to the grind. I don't recommend you gathering 50 essence,
travel to an altar, craft it, and then go out and get another 50, so on and so forth. You want to build up thousands
first, get your XP boost ready like I've said before, pop all your XP boost, take your food, get your food bonuses,
whatever it may be, and then go for manual tunements. And if you want and you want to make it faster but get less
XP, you can just do auto craft. Now, we're going to get into the three combat styles, attack, range, and magic. As I
said, attack is pretty straightforward as you level it by just dealing melee damage to any enemy that you encounter.
And the attack XP that you get is based on the damage you're actually doing with
critical hits to giving you more XP. The biggest thing you want to focus on for attack when you want to boost it and
power level it is you want to go for high health enemies. You don't want to spend half your grind running between
low-level enemies that die in one swing, basically. You want something with enough health that you're constantly
dealing damage as well as applying crit damage to them. Again, this is another skill that I wouldn't just necessarily
grind because you're going to be attacking everything. Part of the game, you're going to be going through fights,
vaults, mini bosses, whatever it may be, and it's just going to level up naturally. Now, once you do finish the
story or you do want to boost to level 99, I recommend you putting on your best melee base gear, use your strongest
upgraded weapon, and farm bosses like world bosses or the end region bosses. Now, one of the best bosses you can
currently farm is either the zogres. Those are really good world bosses, but overall the best boss that you can
repeatedly farm is going to be the Black Knight Titan which you will encounter in doubt on reach. And then any other
repeatable boss because they give you a huge health pool to continuously damage rather than constantly searching for
another enemy after you've killed one. Now, overall, the best target is going to to on your current build and what end
game content you have unlocked already, but the principle doesn't change at all.
Just want maximum damage up time. So, as much damage as you can do in the shortest amount of time, that's pretty
much how you're going to be leveling attack to level 99. Now, just like attack, range works the same way. XP is
based on damage you're dealing with critical damages awarding more XP. Now, one detail to keep in mind is that XP is
capped by the enemy's actual remaining health. So, massively overkilling an enemy, basically, let's say you have a
tier seven sword, and you take out a tier two guy, you're going to be doing way more damage than their health pool,
and you're going to be overkilling these weak enemies, and it's not going to be useful. And again, that's another reason
that high health enemies are much better training targets when you're trying to boost to level 99. And with range, it's
a lot easier to get crits. You have the ability to aim for weak points whenever possible, especially once you're running
a full range armor set, cuz the three-piece set bonus does increase weak point damage. So, you're going to be
able to maximize your XP if you're wearing a full set. And again, for level 99 for range, the same basic rules
apply. Go for the highest damage range setup or your gear set, and then enemies with the largest health pools, and as
little downtime as possible in between. Bosses like dragons throughout the world, dense black knight areas, go to
Daodan Reach and go inside the cathedrals and different areas like that, and go against the black knights,
and repeatable end game encounters all make more sense than shooting a bunch of low-level goblins. Now, one important
difference from several other skills is that there currently isn't a dedicated range XP potion. Your XP setup is more
limited with range itself. You can use the plus 10 knowledgeable nourishment foods, as well as the inspiring range
amulet for another 5%, so you can get a total of 15, but there's not a potion specifically for range that will give
you an XP boost. Keep that in mind. Now, we're on to our last combat style, and this is magic. What you could do is
weaken a bunch of enemies with a sword or a bow, and then once the group is weakened, you could just do a powerful
hit with magic, take all of them out, and you're going to be boosting both those skills at one time. Now, early
game, just use your staff constantly, like I said with every other skill, and work through the elements as you unlock
them. Air is best for control, water allows you to apply a debuff to enemies, which slows them, and it can also drop
healing orb. Then fire is useful because you can apply burn to targets. Now, overall, for magic and dedicated
training of this skill, best thing that I look for is density. Now, Hollows are great for all the undead enemies that
can spawn, and they can spawn constantly in clusters, and they are weak specifically to fire. Now, fights in
Umbral Sands are also very good groups because they give you a lot of enemies clustered together, and basically any
repeatable activity where enemies are being thrown at you constantly is useful because you're reducing the time between
magic kills. Now, just like range, there is currently no dedicated magic XP potion. So, again, you're going to be
using knowledge nourishment, and then inspiring magic amulet to get a total of plus 15 to your XP. Now, what I
recommend, even if you're not a magic user, don't wait until the end of the game to start using magic. Obviously, if
you're in a combat scenario and you're using melee or you're using range, and that's what you like, and you're you
know, you're feeling the flow of the battle, and you just want to take the guy out, that's great. But when you get
the chance to get that final kill shot with magic, I recommend you doing it. Like quickly switch to a stave, switch
to a wand if you want. Wands are introduced in 1.0, they're a lot faster. Just quickly do a you know, quick cast
just to do the final hit on an enemy, and the entire fight you're gaining XP with either range or attack, and then on
the final hit, you're going to be gaining that XP for magic. So, now we are into our last and final, and this is
agility. Now, to me, this is probably the easiest, cleanest, fastest way to get to 99. Cuz the game literally gives
you courses that are designed exactly for this skill and leveling the skill up. Now, you will be gaining a ton of
passive agility XP while you're running around Ashfall and doing whatever you're doing throughout the game. Keep in mind
you only get agility XP when you're on foot. You don't get any when you're using a mount. Overall, this is another
skill that's going to be naturally leveling as you explore through the game. Now, there's five courses
currently in the title. And at level one, which is a chasm dash. Level 15 is the thunder assault. Level 30 is grave
run. 51 is tower climb, and 65 is the lava field. Now, there also is fractured ruins at level 15. Although, thunder
assault is slightly better for repeated training due to the route that that course specifically has. Now, for this
skill, the easiest the skill is very easy and very simple. Every time you unlock a new course, I would go there
immediately and at least run it one time to get your first clear reward. Then, if you're actually pushing to 99, run the
highest course available to you. The higher the course, later the course is in the world's tiers, more XP you're
going to get. Now, agility is a really great skill because it has some of the best quality of life passives that you
can get in the entire game. Level 10 gives you double jump, 32 gives you air dash, 44 gives you phase dash, 50 gives
you backpacker, which it adds another 75 to carry weight, 57 gives you recall, and at 75 you get explorer, which adds
another 75 to carry weight. Now, that means if you don't necessarily care about the 99 cape, getting agility to at
least 75 is incredibly useful for basically every other skill in the title is the extra carry capacity. So, this
could be a skill that you can level up extremely fast if you're just running courses constantly. Even the early game
course, try to get it up to at least level 50 so you get that 75 plus to the carry weight. And then you can start
grinding and farming out all these other skills as you have more carry weight just in general and you have a higher
inventory size. But overall, you know, mounts are fun once you do get them. It it they're going to be fun to use.
You're going to want to use them a lot, but for the most part, you know, throughout early access, for the most
part, we did not have mounts. We had to run everywhere. So, if you're going between two nearby resources, I
recommend you just running because that passive XP is free progression that adds up across an entire play-through. It's
just one of the easiest way to like get the skill up naturally. If you're always
using a mount, you're going to feel that this skill is going to start dragging behind cuz you're not running around as
frequently. Now guys, again, obviously, in Dragon Wilds, you're going to be progressively leveling these skills very
efficiently as you progress through the story, the side quests, and you're just venturing around Ashenfall. But, keep in
mind, if you do want to get to level 99, these are some of the most efficient ways for each skill. And like I said,
there are going to be sometimes where you may boot up the game and you're like, "Today, I want to focus on fishing
because I'm either close to a passive or or close to a spell skill that's going to help me out." And you can use these
methods to then grind them out. At the end of the day, this is one of the best things about Dragon Wilds, in my
opinion. I love survival crafting titles, but this is also what has drawn me so much more into this game
specifically in the genre is the amount of skills and that they give you to work
with and work towards. And it just makes the overall gameplay experience that much more fun. If you guys enjoyed this
video, drop a like on it and subscribe for all things Dragon Wilds. We just hit 20,000 subs. We are on the road to 30K.
We would love to have you in the community. And as always, guys, stay happy, stay hyped, and have a beautiful day.

Some input on better efficiency: 

- Mining: Run entire center-east Fractured Plains and use Rocksplosion on rune essence nodes. Gives 2k+ exp per without any exp boosts and gonna need it for Runecrafting.

- Artisan (as oppose to Arteesan): Just do the merchant method. Setup a large amount of tanning stations and get an easy 500k+ exp per cycle. Not to mention coins for all sort of mats.
- Range/Mage: Setup a Zogre trap/reset method and spam away. Easily fastest for 99.
- Agility: Leave to last skill due to passive exp and do fire trap dodging to finish.
